description: Design an algorithm to encode a list of strings to a single string and decode it back. The encoded string is transmitted over the network and decoded back to the original list.
examples:
Input: ["Hello","World"]
Output: ["Hello","World"]
Explanation: encode then decode returns the original list.
intuition: The challenge is that strings can contain any character, so simple delimiters fail. Length-prefixing solves this elegantly - by writing each string's length before its content, you always know exactly how many characters to read, regardless of what those characters are.
approach: Use length-prefixed encoding: for each string, prepend its length followed by a delimiter character (e.g., "#"). When decoding, read the length, then extract exactly that many characters.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: encode(["Hello","World"])
  "Hello" → "5#Hello"
  "World" → "5#World"
  Encoded: "5#Hello5#World"

decode("5#Hello5#World"):
  readPos=0: delimPos=1, length=5, str="Hello", readPos=7
  readPos=7: delimPos=8, length=5, str="World", readPos=14
  Result: ["Hello","World"]
explanation:
1. Encode: for each string, write its length, a "#" delimiter, then the string itself.
2. Decode: read characters until "#" to get the length.
3. Extract exactly "length" characters after the "#".
4. Move the pointer forward and repeat until the end of the encoded string.
hints: You cannot just use a simple delimiter because the strings may contain any character.
Prefix each string with its length so you know exactly how many characters to read.
Use a separator between the length and the string content.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: S = total payload characters; H = total length-prefix and delimiter characters; C = S + H = encoded length.
timeComplexityBreakdown.title: encode
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Prefix overhead matters even when every input string is empty.

operations.title: decode

phases.label: Read and parse all length prefixes

operations.note: The read position advances past each decoded string. Characters are not rescanned from the beginning.
